summary: The milestone completed 10 experiments in 7 minutes, including 4 compute-bound tasks. The two longest compute-bound entries were each reported at 2 minutes; compute-bound GPU idle was false, and the supplied data does not establish a concurrent multi-model task that should have used DualGPURunner.
bottlenecks_identified: The Gated calibration-only authentic Phase-D candidate pool and Phase-D task-scoped GPU engagement and sealed-ladder canary were the longest compute-bound entries at 2 minutes each, but the supplied timing data has no phase breakdown that explains why.
Disk-modification-time reconstruction provides coarse experiment durations rather than setup, model-load, inference, and teardown timing, limiting causal bottleneck attribution.
Task-level concurrent model counts and runner-selection traces are absent, so DualGPURunner applicability cannot be audited from the supplied data.
improvements_suggested: Emit phase timestamps and task-correlated GPU utilization samples for every compute-bound experiment.
Stamp model count, model-overlap interval, and selected runner in each compute-bound artifact so DualGPURunner applicability is explicit.
Add a scheduler hint that offers the unused GPU to an independent compute-bound job; keep single-model tasks on one GPU and require DualGPURunner only when at least 2 models are loaded in parallel.
Prefer live task timestamps over disk-modification-time reconstruction for milestone timing.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add per-phase timing and task-scoped GPU telemetry to compute-bound experiment artifacts.
Schedule independent compute-bound jobs onto separate GPUs when concurrency and memory checks pass.
Record concurrent model count and runner selection so multi-model DualGPURunner misses are directly detectable.
meta_reflection: The monitor snapshot showed GPU 0 in use at 29% utilization while GPU 1 was idle, but the locked task classification reports no compute-bound GPU-idle fault. That snapshot establishes engagement rather than task-lifetime efficiency, and it does not prove that the second GPU had eligible parallel work. The 29% savings estimate is an upper bound from overlapping one reported 2-minute compute-bound entry within the 7-minute wall time; task independence is not supplied, so the estimate is not a measured speedup.
